name: Farringdon - Liverpool Street (Elizabeth line corridor), London
description: Ground along a 2.1 km corridor of the Elizabeth line between Farringdon and Liverpool Street, from 14 open BGS/Crossrail boreholes.
datum: m OD (ground levels of the logs; datum not stated in the files, values fit m OD)
licence: Borehole data: Open Government Licence v3.0. Contains British Geological Survey materials (c) UKRI 2026. Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.

MG.name: Made Ground
MG.source: Chandegra & Kokkinou (2016), Crossrail Learning Legacy, Design of the deep cut-and-cover Crossrail Paddington Station, Table 1, https://learninglegacy.crossrail.co.uk/documents/design-deep-cut-cover-crossrail-paddington-station-using-finite-element-method/
MG.notes: PAD prints c' 20 kPa; 0 is used. K0 = K0nc 0.577.

AL.name: Alluvium
AL.notes: Soft, normally consolidated, with peat (BGS); no open parameters found, values assumed.

RTD.name: River Terrace Deposits (gravel)
RTD.source: Chandegra & Kokkinou (2016), Crossrail Learning Legacy, Design of the deep cut-and-cover Crossrail Paddington Station, Table 1, https://learninglegacy.crossrail.co.uk/documents/design-deep-cut-cover-crossrail-paddington-station-using-finite-element-method/

LC.name: London Clay Formation
LC.source: Chandegra & Kokkinou (2016), Crossrail Learning Legacy, Design of the deep cut-and-cover Crossrail Paddington Station, Table 1, https://learninglegacy.crossrail.co.uk/documents/design-deep-cut-cover-crossrail-paddington-station-using-finite-element-method/; K0 and pore pressure: Wan, Standing, Potts & Burland (2019), Geotechnique 69(5):434-457, doi:10.1680/jgeot.17.P.309 (CC BY 4.0), Table 2 and p. 440
LC.notes: K0 1.5: top of the central-London design range 1.0-1.5 quoted in Wan et al.; measured 1.9-2.4 at 29-35 m (Hyde Park). Pore pressure about 0.9 x hydrostatic at Hyde Park (under-drained), derived from Wan et al. Table 2. cu = 83.1 + 7.4 z kPa (z below the top of the clay; Brosse et al. 2025, ISGSR, doi:10.3850/GRF-25280825_isgsr-185-P110-cd).

HF.name: Harwich Formation (basal London Clay sands and gravels)
HF.source: Environment Agency (2022), Management of the London Basin Chalk Aquifer, status report, https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/london-basin-chalk-aquifer-annual-status-report (OGL)
HF.notes: Part of the Chalk-Basal Sands aquifer (EA); no open strength or stiffness, values assumed like Upnor sand (LG Table 6.7).

LG.name: Lambeth Group
LG.source: Entwisle et al. (2013), BGS OR/13/006, Engineering Geology of British Rocks and Soils: Lambeth Group, https://nora.nerc.ac.uk/id/eprint/503110/
LG.notes: Bulk density medians 2.04-2.08 Mg/m3 (6.1.1); c', phi' of Reading Formation clay, triaxial (Table 6.7). Under-drained by the Thanet Sand and Chalk in central London (p. 186), but sand channels can hold high water pressure. K0 2.5 measured at Limehouse (7.3.5); 1.5 assumed. Drained E assumed.

TS.name: Thanet Sand Formation
TS.source: Menkiti et al. (2015), Crossrail Learning Legacy, Geology and geotechnical properties of the Thanet Sand Formation, section 4, https://learninglegacy.crossrail.co.uk/documents/geology-geotechnical-properties-thanet-sand-formation-update-crossrail-project-2/
TS.notes: Bulk density 1.88-1.9 Mg/m3, c' 0, peak phi' 37-39 deg at 400-700 kPa (4.1-4.2). K0 and E only in figures there; assumed.

CK.name: Chalk
CK.notes: UCS 1.25-5 MPa saturated (BGS); no open strength or stiffness parameters, values assumed.

alignment.source: Assumed. Depth and geology at Farringdon: Crossrail Learning Legacy, Tunnelling in sand in Farringdon Crossrail Station, https://learninglegacy.crossrail.co.uk/documents/tunnelling-sand-farringdon-crossrail-station/; Geotechnical risk management for SCL tunnels in Farringdon, https://learninglegacy.crossrail.co.uk/documents/geotechnical-risk-management-for-sprayed-concrete-lining-tunnels-in-farringdon-crossrail-station/

groundwater.source: Water strikes in the BGS/Crossrail borehole logs (WSTG/WSTD); Environment Agency (2022), Management of the London Basin Chalk Aquifer, status report, https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/london-basin-chalk-aquifer-annual-status-report (OGL)
groundwater.notes: Strike readings, not equilibrium levels. London Clay pore pressure 0.9 x hydrostatic on the upper table.
